system_name.reference: We introduce the novel approach of recursively embedding, clustering, and summarizing chunks of text, constructing a tree with differing levels of summarization from the bottom up. At inference time, our RAPTOR model retrieves from this tree

system_category.reference: Retrieval-augmented language models can better adapt to changes in world state and incorporate long-tail knowledge. However, most existing methods retrieve only short contiguous chunks from a retrieval corpus, limiting holistic understanding of the overall document context.

knowledge_representation.reference: Construction of the RAPTOR tree begins with segmenting the retrieval corpus into short, contiguous texts of length 100, similar to traditional retrieval augmentation techniques. If a sentence exceeds the 100-token limit, we move the entire sentence to the next chunk
